Subject: Operator custody & escrow-like options for private deployment

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the HelioWell infra team is positive about Redwood but legal/procurement have flagged the private deployment custody language as a blocker. Two specific asks from our side:

1) Operator activity and access model: we need explicit limits on what Redwood operators can do if you provide assistance for on-prem or VPC installs (console ssh, snapshot pulls, remote exec).
2) Escrow-like evidence pathway: our security team wants a defensible pathway to get a sealed snapshot or cryptographic attestation if Redwood goes insolvent or cannot provide support. They called it an "escrow-lite" scenario.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports: staged witness snapshots, third-party sealed custody, or time-limited console witness sessions? Also, can you share sample MSA/Exhibit language we can present to our counsel?

I attached our hosting checklist for reference (high level). We're aiming to finalize order form and exhibits by end of next month.

Attachments: HelioWell-ThirdParty-Hosting-Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

Next best step: a short call between legal teams this week would help. Availability: Wed-Fri mornings PST.

Amelia — thanks for the checklist and clear asks. Quick summary of practical, production-friendly options Redwood can offer; I captured pros/cons so you can share with counsel: 

1) Steward-in-place (Default): Redwood operates support services but does NOT hold customer data in our KMS for private deployments unless explicitly agreed. Operators access is strictly via audited runbooks; privileged console sessions are time-limited and recorded. Pros: fastest recovery. Cons: requires trust in our ops procedures.

2) Escrow-lite (recommended for regulated customers): Redwood generates an encrypted snapshot and deposits a sealed package with a neutral custodian (third-party) plus cryptographic attestation. Custodian releases only on pre-defined triggers (insolvency, failure to meet SLA for X days). Pros: strong for legal teams. Cons: additional cost and setup time.

3) Operator-limited witness: Redwood performs live witness sessions for restore/validation with customer or third-party auditor present; we provide tamper-evident logs and an exportable signed manifest. Pros: lower cost vs full escrow.

If helpful, I attached a short explainer doc (escrow-lite-options.docx) and a proposed timeline (we estimate 3–4 weeks to operationalize an escrow-lite offer).

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa / Redwood legal to draft sample Exhibit language for each path (we think HelioWell will prefer option 2 or 3).
- 30-minute legal sync Thurs 12/17 or Fri 12/18 (morning PST).

If those slots don't work, propose alternatives.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operator custody & escrow-like options for private deployment

Hi Amelia / Sofia — looping in legal. High-level reactions after an initial read:

- We can support both Escrow-lite and Operator-limited witness. I pushed back on any language that gives the customer unilateral right to retrieve snapshots without the trigger framework — that undermines customer data controls.
- Proposed redlines I want to surface before the sync: add a defined "Custody Trigger" section (examples: insolvency, sustained failure to meet documented SLA for 30 calendar days, or court order). Add a requirement that any handback is accompanied by a certified forensic manifest and remote witness session.
- Audit window: propose a 30-day scheduled witnessing window plus a one-time emergency 5-day window for incident response.
- Logs & evidence: we can commit to retaining access logs and KMS attestation records for 12 months (subject to Order Form).

Attached: MSA_Annex_Custody_redline_v1.pdf (pdf) and orderform-sample-exhibit.docx (docx) — redline contains inline language for Exhibit X and a short fallback paragraph to the hosted API if the trigger is met but handback is infeasible.

David — can you confirm whether the proposed "Custody Trigger" formulation is acceptable from a legal/risk perspective and if we should require escrow custodian accreditation (e.g., SOC 2 Type II)?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: MSA_Annex_Custody_redline_v1.pdf, orderform-sample-exhibit.docx

Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operator custody & escrow-like options for private deployment

Amelia — thanks for the patience. After review, legal is comfortable with the Escrow-lite pathway subject to the following guardrails (draft clause excerpt below). I also added a short acceptance timeline so procurement can proceed.

---
Draft Exhibit E (Custody & Witnessing) — excerpt

1. Definitions: "Custody Trigger" means (a) Redwood insolvency or cessation of business operations; (b) Redwood failure to cure a material SLA breach within 30 calendar days following written notice; or (c) a final, non-appealable court order compelling release.

2. Escrow-lite mechanism: Upon a Custody Trigger, Redwood shall cause an encrypted snapshot and associated cryptographic manifest to be released by the designated third-party custodian to HelioWell or its designee, pursuant to a mutually executed release protocol. Release shall be accompanied by a signed forensic manifest and a one-time assisted restoration witness session.

3. Custodian accreditation & retention: The designated custodian must maintain SOC 2 Type II or equivalent and shall retain sealed artifacts for a minimum of 90 days. Access logs and KMS attestation records will be retained by Redwood for 12 months.

4. Fallback: If release is infeasible due to technical constraints, Redwood will provide a prioritized support pathway to enable HelioWell to recover service via a hosted fallback endpoint within an agreed timeline.

---

Comments / next steps:
- We recommend adding the above excerpt as Exhibit E and referencing it from the Order Form.
- Please review the attached redline (I incorporated Marissa's notes) and confirm whether HelioWell requires the custodian to be pre-named in the Order Form or whether a specification of accreditation is sufficient.
- Proposed internal timeline: Redwood legal to finalize Exhibit text by 12/27; commercial to circulate final Order Form by 01/03/2027; target signature by 01/17/2027.

Related links: DocuSign pre-authoring envelope (https://docusign.com/req/abc123-RW-HELI-4729) and a draft folder for evidence artifacts (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-privdeploy-evidence).
